notes.author: agent:claude
notes.text: Recorded measurements are about 67 to 68 MiB for the controller against roughly 60 MiB for a bare Node HTTP process on the reference host. The 50 MiB target is below the runtime floor, so the release validation of the main feature item cannot pass as written regardless of how efficient the controller becomes.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Fold this small measurement/documentation correction into verification of the refresh and log fixes. Historical 67-68 MiB versus roughly 60 MiB baseline numbers are reference measurements, not current guarantees. Agree a reproducible overhead/growth budget from fresh data; no runtime migration or host-policy change is authorized.

problem: Top-level architecture/product documents still state an absolute 50 MiB idle RSS target. Historical reference-host measurements were about 67-68 MiB for the controller versus roughly 60 MiB for a bare Node process, so that target did not measure the controller's own overhead.
The integrated switching item now explicitly defers to this measurement procedure; documentation and a fresh reproducible baseline still need to be reconciled.
scope: Replace the absolute idle RSS target with controller overhead measured above a bare Node baseline process on the same host and runtime version, or raise the absolute budget to a value the runtime can meet, and state which was chosen and why.
Define the measurement procedure explicitly: runtime version, build, number of registered projects, idle duration before sampling, and which memory metric is sampled.

Reconcile the current product/architecture documentation and integrated switching acceptance criteria with the revised procedure. Preserve historical measurement notes as dated evidence; archived notes must not be interpreted as current budgets.
Keep the intent intact: the controller must remain unnoticeable next to the development servers it supervises, so idle CPU and bounded log memory stay in the acceptance set.
title: Revise the unreachable idle memory acceptance target
validation: Measure a bare Node HTTP baseline and the release controller on the same host and runtime, and verify the revised criterion is met with margin and is reproducible across runs.
Verify the revised criterion still fails a deliberately regressed build, for example one that retains unbounded log buffers or polls Git continuously.
Verify active project documents and acceptance criteria agree on the current budget and measurement procedure; superseded numbers may remain only as clearly dated historical evidence.
value: Release verification measures what the project actually cares about, the controller's own overhead, instead of failing on a floor imposed by the Node runtime.
